thread:
emma_sales: NorthStar Health POC request: they want Redwood Private inside their VPC. Requirements: no public egress from data plane, prefer PrivateLink/interface VPCE, want mutual TLS between their service and our endpoint, and a small dedicated pool for a 48h trial (hourly). Also asking for a scoped hosted API key that can be rotated every 7 days.
ryan_neteng: Ok. PrivateLink + interface endpoints is the cleanest for zero-egress. Important DNS pieces: have them create a Private Hosted Zone (e.g. api.redwood-private.internal) or enable the VPCE 'Private DNS' option so our service name resolves to the VPCE IPs. If they have TGW with restricted propagation, they'll need explicit route entries to the subnets hosting the VPCE ENIs.
paul_se: For the API key we can issue a project-scoped key (project:northstar-poc) and bind it to the VPCE-id(s) for stronger scoping. We can also provide short-lived tokens (STS-like) for their SDKs. 7-day rotation is fine for POC.
emma_sales: they specifically asked about mTLS cert exchange and cert rotation cadence. They want to present a client cert from their side. Can we support client cert validation on the PrivateLink?
leo_ops: We support mutual TLS at the frontend for Private customers. We need them to upload the client certs (or a CA chain) and indicate rotation window. Ops will wire the cert into the gateway for the POC. Also need to know whether they want client cert auth only or cert + API key.
nina_sec: Security checklist: 1) No NAT/IGW on data subnets, 2) VPCE interface endpoints only in private subnets, 3) KMS CMK for logs if they want CMEK, send ARN, 4) CloudTrail + VPC Flow Logs to their logging account, 5) API key rotation policy (7d), 6) Audit retention window for POC (recommend 30d). Also recommend role-based SAML read-only access if they want to view usage in console.
ryan_neteng: Minimal route table example for a subnet hosting VPCE ENIs (they can adapt for TGW):
```
# Route table for app subnet with interface VPCE
Destination     Target
10.1.0.0/16     local
10.200.0.0/16   tgw-attach (if needed)
# don't add 0.0.0.0/0 if you require no internet egress
```
And example security group snippet: allow outbound TCP 443 to our VPCE service and inbound from internal CIDR for test instances.
```
# SG rules (conceptual)
Inbound: 10.1.10.0/24 TCP 443
Outbound: 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443 (or restrict to our vpce ip range if they have it)
```
paul_se: If they want IP-level allowlisting instead of VPCE binding, provide their account's NAT/egress IPs. Note: interface endpoints use ENIs in their subnet so traffic originates from those ENI IPs. We can provide expected ENI prefixes but binding to VPCE-id is cleaner.
emma_sales: Billing side: can we short-term carve 2x A10G and bill hourly? They need to know cost estimate before thumb-up.
leo_ops: We can carve a temporary dedicated slice (2x A10G) for 48h. Ops will tag the resources and mark a billing object as hourly for this carve. Finance must approve a one-off hourly billing or we apply credits. ETA for carve: ~3-6 hours depending on region capacity. I'll open the ops ticket once we have account ID.
deploy-bot: Provision job queued: POC_POOL_NORTHSTAR_1752468000 - requested 2xA10G. Status: queued. ETA 4h.
emma_sales: Can you provide the simple curl test I'll ask them to run from an instance in the subnet to confirm private DNS + TLS?
ryan_neteng: Example smoke test using internal FQDN (assuming Private DNS enabled):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-private.internal/v1/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SCOPED_KEY>' --cert client.crt --key client.key
```
Expect 200 and a small JSON payload. If they get TLS errors, check that Private DNS resolves to the interface IP and that SG allows outbound 443.
nina_sec: Also: ask for their split-horizon DNS setup details. If they override internal resolver, their resolver must prefer the Private Hosted Zone. If they use forwarders, ensure conditional forward to the VPC resolver.
paul_se: Final note on keys: we'll provide the scoped hosted key and also an endpoint-bound key option. We'll send ephemeral SDK tokens for integration tests to avoid sharing long-lived credentials.
emma_sales: Great, I'll send a short doc with these steps and request: account ID, VPC ID, target subnet IDs (where to create VPCE), whether they want mTLS only or mTLS+API key, and decision on hourly billing vs credit. Thanks team :thumbsup:
